---
name: lumen-adapter-accumulator-real-data-gaps
description: "Inventory of Lumen adapter/accumulator design decisions made from inference rather than verified real session data, discovered 2026-08-20 -- needed before any further Lumen spec/implementation work."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 36644eef-36d9-4e53-b672-5ddcebfc54f0
  modified: 2026-08-20T22:12:18.276Z
---

On 2026-08-20, after believing Lumen's `SPEC-002-SESSION`/`SPEC-005-ANALYSIS` work was solid (green tests, adversarial-reviewed plan), a user question ("what does Kimi/Qwen use for session info?") led to checking real session files on disk instead of guessing, which cascaded into finding that several "verified" designs were never checked against real data — only checked for internal self-consistency (code matches its own spec criterion), which is a much weaker claim.

## Confirmed wrong (not just narrow) -- needs a real rewrite, not a patch

- **`CodexAdapter`** (`crates/lumen-session/src/adapters/codex.rs`): built on an assumed raw-OpenAI-Chat-Completions-API shape (`choices[].message`, `usage.prompt_tokens`). Real Codex CLI rollout files (`~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl`) use a completely different envelope format: `{timestamp, ordinal, type, payload}`, with `event_msg/token_count` for cumulative usage and `response_item/message` + `custom_tool_call`/`custom_tool_call_output` (or a second, distinct `function_call`/`function_call_output` pair) for turns. Verified directly against a real, live local session file.
- **`OpenCodeAdapter`**: built on an assumed `action`/`observation`/`source` JSONL shape with **zero basis in any real OpenCode version, ever** (confirmed via CodeBurn's own source comment). Real OpenCode has exactly two generations: legacy file-based JSON (`storage/session|message|part/*.json`, pre-1.1) and current SQLite (`session`/`message`/`part` tables, verified directly via `sqlite3` on a real local `opencode.db`). Both share one `role`/`type` shape neither matches Lumen's assumption.
- **`HookActivityAccumulator`** (`crates/lumen-analysis/src/accumulators/hook_activity.rs`, spec'd as `CRIT-LUMEN-139`/`140`): field names (`hookEventName`, `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`, `permissionDecision`) were inferred from "general knowledge," never checked against a real hook-execution record. ## External research wave, part 2, 2026-08-20 (LangSmith evaluation-concepts/observability, IBM/TDS/Elastic/Splunk LLM-observability overviews, real OTel GenAI semantic conventions, academic literature)

- **The single most important finding of the whole research wave: both `otel_request_ids` (on `CanonicalTranscript`) and `otel_span_id` (on `CanonicalToolResult`) are structurally wrong relative to the real, authoritative spec** (`github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai`), not just unpopulated placeholders. The real correlator is `gen_ai.conversation.id` -- one singular ID per *session*, attached to many per-call spans -- not a small list collected at the transcript level. `gen_ai.response.id` is per-call and would belong on `CanonicalTurn`, not the transcript. `otel_span_id` conflates a real distributed-tracing span ID (16-hex protocol identifier -- a materially bigger, currently-unscoped feature) with what `SpanMappingAccumulator` actually tries to do (correlate a tool call to something), which already has an answer: `gen_ai.tool.call.id` is functionally identical to Lumen's *existing* `call_id` field -- `SpanMappingAccumulator` may not need to exist as currently conceived. One good side-effect: `gen_ai.agent.name`/`gen_ai.workflow.name` are a clean, ecosystem-agnostic answer to the `AttributionSource::{Plugin,Skill}` taxonomy problem (ties two separate gaps into one fix), and `gen_ai.conversation.compacted` is a standard way to represent what Lumen's PreCompact snapshot-merge logic already does internally. Tool calls are a separate span type from inference calls in the real spec; MCP tool calls have their own dedicated conventions file.
- **Industry-standard LLM observability pillars** (synthesized from IBM/TDS/Elastic/Splunk, IBM's own page 403-blocked): functional/performance (Lumen covers well), input monitoring (prompt-injection, adversarial detection -- Lumen has none), output monitoring (hallucination/toxicity/PII/groundedness scoring -- Lumen has none, the single largest missing category), security/compliance (none), embeddings-based anomaly detection (Lumen's Tarjan-SCC is a structurally different, graph-based alternative -- legitimate, not a gap), MELT framework with **OpenTelemetry explicitly named the emerging standard** (validates the otel_* direction even though the fields themselves need the redesign above), RAG metrics (not applicable). **Correctly scoped, not a Lumen defect**: pillars 2-4 (input/output/security) are arguably Prism's job (grading correctness/safety), not Lumen's (which measures efficiency/trajectory) -- a real system-level gap between the two projects, not something to bolt onto Lumen's accumulators. Two industry-wide caveats worth knowing: no established best practice exists yet for alert-threshold tuning (Lumen's unvalidated `SPEC-007` thresholds are in good company, not uniquely bad), and manual review of 50-100 samples remains a best-practice baseline industry-wide -- Lumen has no human-in-the-loop mechanism anywhere.
- **LangSmith evaluation-concepts/observability** (deeper than the eval/insights docs already noted above): vocabulary is `Run` (execution trace, no reference output) / `Example` (inputs + optional reference output) / `Dataset` (collection of Examples) / `Evaluator` (dual-mode: `(example,run)` offline, `(run)` alone online) -- "Trace" itself is used loosely, closer to what Lumen calls `CanonicalTranscript` than a distinct type. Confirms (a second independent time, alongside CodeBurn) that clustering-based session classification, not fixed ratio-thresholds, is the real industry pattern -- LangSmith's own Insights does "unsupervised topic clustering." One point *in Lumen's favor*: LangSmith's anomaly detection is generic ("flag unusual patterns"), no named mechanism -- Lumen's `TrajectoryAnomaly` enum (`CircularLoop`/`ContextFlood`/`GateStall`/`UngroundedDrafting`) is more specific and algorithmically defined.
- **Academic literature** (arXiv, 2026): `RedundancyBench` (arXiv:2605.29893) formalizes exactly what Lumen's Tarjan-SCC cycle detection approximates, with a more rigorous per-step-contribution-labeling methodology to validate against instead of a fixed cycle-depth->=3 threshold. `Graphectory` encodes trajectories as graphs for process-centric (not just outcome) metrics -- same design space as Lumen's `TrajectoryGraph`, worth reading directly. The field has broadly moved to process-level not just outcome-level evaluation (SWE-Bench Pro, SWE Atlas, AgentLens's "Lucky Pass Problem" -- an agent can pass via wrong-reasoning path), validating Prism's `RedGreenGrader`+`TrajectoryGrader` combination directionally. **For Prism's unbuilt `CalibratedJudge`**: a large systematic study (arXiv:2606.19544, 21 judges/9 providers/~541K judgments) found judge rankings shift up to 14 positions across benchmarks, and critically that **high test-retest reliability (>0.95) can coexist with severe position bias (>0.10)** -- a judge can look stable while being systematically biased by anchor ordering -- and that naive exact-match agreement overstates discriminative ability by 33-41 percentage points once bias-corrected. `CalibraEval` (arXiv:2410.15393) is a specific, citable calibration technique. Verdict: the planned "contrastive few-shot anchors" design is on the right track but needs explicit anchor-order randomization and calibration, not just anchors alone, or it will likely reproduce this exact failure mode.

## External research wave, part 3, 2026-08-20 -- comparable open source projects (ccusage, Langfuse, OpenLLMetry, OpenHands)

User asked "what other open source projects are doing something similar." Four parallel forks, each scoped to one project with an explicit "research only, cite real files, don't overstate coverage" instruction (per [[feedback-verify-fork-scope-and-stats]]). All four returned concrete, file-cited findings -- no vague synthesis.

**Convergent lessons -- the same conclusion reached independently by 2-3 unrelated real systems, which is stronger evidence than any single source:**

- **Multi-level/tree-structured agent hierarchy is real, confirmed three independent ways.** Langfuse's `observations` table has a self-referencing nullable `parent_observation_id` (arbitrary depth, not a fixed enum of levels). OpenHands' native `Event` model has an explicit `parent_id` forming a tree, with delegated sub-agents themselves able to delegate further (capped by `max_children`, default 5) -- directly contradicts `CircuitBreakerAccumulator`'s single-level `parent->{agent_type}` string-key model, which structurally cannot represent nesting or multiple distinct children. `ccusage`'s real Claude adapter independently confirms a live top-level `is_sidechain: bool` field on real Claude Code JSONL entries plus subagent transcripts living in sibling files (`<project>/<session>/subagents/<worker>.jsonl`) -- this needs a real redesign, not a patch, and now has three independent reference shapes to design against.
- **Hook telemetry as a first-class separate event/span type, confirmed a second independent way.** OpenHands has a native `HookExecutionEvent` (`hook_event_type: PreToolUse|PostToolUse|UserPromptSubmit|SessionStart|SessionEnd|Stop`, `blocked`, `exit_code`) as its own event class, not embedded in message text -- this is a second, structurally unrelated confirmation (native framework event model, not OTel spans) of the same conclusion the VS Code/Copilot OTel research already reached. Two independent real systems agree: `HookActivityAccumulator` was looking in the wrong place (transcript text) for something that genuinely exists elsewhere as its own event stream, not that it doesn't exist.
- **Cost/pricing data should be a data table (queryable, versioned), not a hardcoded match statement -- confirmed two independent ways, one with a dimension Lumen hasn't considered at all.** Langfuse has real Postgres `Model`/`Price`/`PricingTier` tables joined on `internal_model_id`, plus open `Map(String, ...)` usage/cost fields (not fixed columns) so new token categories need no schema migration. `ccusage`'s Kimi adapter goes further: pricing is **timestamp-gated** -- a hardcoded cutoff switches which model a generic display name (`kimi-for-coding`) resolves to for pricing purposes. Lumen's flat `pricing.rs` match statement needs both a live/queryable-table redesign AND a temporal dimension, not just updated numbers.
- **Pluggable/priority-ordered mapping registries for heterogeneous producers of a nominally-standard format, confirmed real and necessary.** Langfuse's real OTel ingestion (`OtelIngestionProcessor.ts` + `ObservationTypeMapper.ts`) is a priority-ordered registry of `SimpleAttributeMapper`/`CustomAttributeMapper` instances specifically because different SDKs emit `gen_ai.*` spans differently -- direct validation for the pluggable-validator-registry redesign already proposed for `SchemaExtractorAccumulator`. Same underlying problem, independently solved the same way by a mature production system.
- **Idempotent last-write-wins ingestion is the real, proven answer to session-forking/replay double-counting.** Langfuse's ClickHouse tables use `ReplacingMergeTree(event_ts, is_deleted)` specifically for out-of-order/duplicate/updated events -- a concrete, adoptable pattern for the `CodexAdapter` forked-session double-counting risk flagged earlier, not a hypothetical concern to design around from scratch.
- **Malformed-line handling is industry-standard silent-skip, not uniquely a Lumen shortcut -- but that doesn't excuse it.** `ccusage`'s `common/jsonl.rs:61` does exactly what Lumen's `claude.rs:60-66` does (`.ok()`-and-continue on parse failure, no recorded warning). Confirms `CRIT-LUMEN-025`'s overclaim is a real, common gap worth fixing (RTK's `parse_failures` table remains the validated pattern to fix it with), not something to feel uniquely bad about.

**A real, load-bearing spec-vs-shipped-code gap, from reading actual production instrumentation rather than the spec alone:**

- OpenLLMetry's real Anthropic instrumentation (`span_utils.py`) **never sets `gen_ai.conversation.id`** anywhere -- confirms it's aspirational at the provider-instrumentation layer (a raw Anthropic API call has no concept of "conversation" to attach). `gen_ai.response.id` **is** populated in practice, matching spec.
- MCP tool-call spans (`opentelemetry-instrumentation-mcp`) get their own dedicated child span (correct, matches the spec's tool-calls-are-a-separate-span-type model) but populate it with **zero official `gen_ai.tool.*` attributes** -- instead using OpenLLMetry's own proprietary `TRACELOOP_SPAN_KIND`/`TRACELOOP_ENTITY_NAME` vocabulary. A `SpanMappingAccumulator` built strictly against the official registry fields would miss how the most popular real OTel GenAI instrumentation library actually tags the exact span type it's meant to correlate.
- OpenLLMetry's own `MIGRATION.md` documents that even within one vendor's code, exact attribute string values have changed across versions (`gen_ai.usage.cache_creation_input_tokens` -> `gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.input_tokens`; `gen_ai.system` value case changed `"Anthropic"` -> `"anthropic"`) -- concretely validates the registry's own `stability: development` caveat as more than a formality.
- **Implication for the redesign already planned**: build the OTel correlation layer as a tolerant/adapter-pattern consumer (mirroring Langfuse's mapper-registry approach above), not a strict schema match against the official registry -- the registry describes the aspiration, not universally what ships.

**New concrete facts about specific formats, several directly closing previously-open questions:**

Four independent real implementations, four different answers. Its record shape aliases many field names per token count (`input`/`prompt`/`input_tokens`/`prompt_tokens`...), suggesting upstream Gemini CLI's own schema isn't stable either -- this may be a moving target, not a single answer waiting to be found.

## The `~/.gemini/logs/` provenance mystery is now FULLY RESOLVED, 2026-08-20

Root cause: Google discontinued Gemini CLI as a consumer product, replacing it with **Antigravity CLI**, per the official Google Developers Blog (`developers.googleblog.com/an-important-update-transitioning-gemini-cli-to-antigravity-cli/`, verified directly, not secondhand) -- Antigravity CLI became available to everyone on **2026-05-19**, and Gemini CLI/Gemini Code Assist stopped serving Pro/Ultra and free-tier requests on **2026-06-18** (enterprise-licensed users retain Gemini CLI access). Antigravity spans three real, distinct local products sharing the parent `~/.gemini` namespace, all confirmed present on this machine: `~/.gemini/antigravity/` (the IDE), `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/` (the CLI, aka `agy`), `~/.gemini/antigravity-ide/`. This explains exactly why four independent sources (CodeBurn's two providers, `agent-session-parser`, `ccusage`'s Gemini adapter reading `~/.gemini/tmp/`) all disagreed -- each was written against a different product/era in a fast-moving transition, not this current shape. This machine's session data (dated late July/August 2026) is post-transition, current ground truth.

**The `~/.gemini/logs/*.jsonl` files earlier flagged as "provenance unconfirmed" are literally symlinks**, confirmed via `ls -la`: `~/.gemini/logs/<conversation-id>.jsonl -> ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<conversation-id>/.system_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl`. `logs/` is a convenience flattening layer, not a source of truth in its own right -- adapters should target the `brain/` path.

**Real transcript.jsonl schema, read directly (not inferred)**: one JSON object per line, fields `step_index` (int), `source` (`USER_EXPLICIT` | `MODEL`), `type` (a rich per-action enum: `USER_INPUT`, `LIST_DIRECTORY`, `VIEW_FILE`, `PLANNER_RESPONSE`, others uncatalogued), `status` (`DONE`, others uncatalogued), `created_at` (ISO 8601), `content` (text; for tool-action entries, this is the serialized tool result, not a separate structured result field). `PLANNER_RESPONSE` entries additionally carry `thinking` (reasoning text) and `tool_calls[]` (`name` + `args`, with `args` values themselves JSON-encoded as strings, e.g. `"args":{"DirectoryPath":"\"/Users/gabe/...\""}` -- double-encoded, a real parsing gotcha). This is structurally an Action/Observation-per-type-class model (closer to OpenHands' native model, `type` names the operation, not the message role) -- NOT the `step_index`/`source`/`type` triple in the shape Lumen's existing `AgyAdapter`/`detect_orchestrator` code was built against; the field *names* happen to overlap but the *value vocabulary* was never actually enumerated before now and needs to be checked against the adapter's current match arms.

**Two more real, distinct file shapes for the same conversation, previously unknown:** (1) a sibling `<id>.json` (no `l`) file -- a single JSON object with `sessionId`/`title`/`prompt`/`summary`/`turns[]`, where each turn is `{role, parts: [{text}]}` -- this is the standard Gemini API `Content`/`Part` shape, a precomputed summary/index view, structurally different from the raw `transcript.jsonl` and likely easier to parse if only turn-level (not full tool-call) fidelity is needed. (2) `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/history.jsonl` -- a flat *command-input* history log (`display`, `timestamp` as epoch-millis, `workspace`, `conversationId`, optional `type:"slash_command"`), NOT a conversation transcript -- a third, unrelated artifact type in the same product, useful only for correlating raw user keystrokes/slash-commands to a `conversationId`, not for turn/token reconstruction.

## Pricing architecture decision, 2026-08-20 -- the "exchange rate" model

User proposed, and this is now the settled design direction: **accumulators/adapters should only ever store raw usage data (token counts per category, model name as reported, timestamp) -- never a computed cost.** Cost is derived downstream via a lookup against a **versioned rate table**: rows of `(model, token_type, provider?, rate_per_unit, effective_from, effective_until_nullable)`, looked up by **the turn's own timestamp, not "now"** -- exactly like looking up a historical FX rate for a past transaction, not today's rate. This directly resolves two things found in this research wave, not a novel idea invented in isolation: Langfuse's real schema already separates raw `usage_details`/`cost_details` (open maps) from a separate queryable `Model`/`Price`/`PricingTier` table; `ccusage`'s Kimi adapter already has to do a timestamp-gated cutoff for one specific case (`KIMI_FOR_CODING_K2_6_CUTOFF_MS`) precisely because it lacks a general versioned-rate mechanism and has to hand-code the cutoff instead. This is the general form of that same problem. Practical implications for the redesign: (1) keep any provider-reported cost field (e.g. Claude Code's real `costUSD`) alongside the independently-computed one, not instead of it, mirroring Langfuse's `provided_*`-raw-vs-canonicalized twin-field pattern, so the two can be cross-checked for drift; (2) `pricing.rs`'s fix is this architectural separation, not just refreshed numbers -- the current hardcoded match-statement can't represent a rate change over time at all, which is a real, now-confirmed-necessary case, not a hypothetical one; (3) OpenRouter/LiteLLM's live feeds (already researched) become periodic snapshot sources that insert new `effective_from`-stamped rows, never overwrite old ones -- this is what makes historical cost analysis correct even after a provider changes prices.

## Where real data / reference implementations live (as of 2026-08-20)

- Real Codex CLI sessions: `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl`
- Real OpenCode sessions: `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (SQLite; `session`/`message`/`part`/`event` tables)
- Real Antigravity CLI sessions (provenance fully resolved -- see dedicated section above): `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<conversation-id>/.system_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl` (raw, real ground truth; `~/.gemini/logs/*.jsonl` are symlinks to this), plus sibling `~/.gemini/logs/<id>.json` (precomputed turn-level summary) and `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/history.jsonl` (unrelated command-input log)
- Real Claude Code sessions (including this very session's own transcript): `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl`
- **CodeBurn** (`github.com/getagentseal/codeburn`, MIT licensed, npm/npx installable): a real, production, multi-orchestrator on-disk session parser covering 37 tools via `src/providers/*.ts` (includes `codex.ts`, `opencode.ts`, `opencode-file-parser.ts`, `antigravity.ts`, `claude.ts`, `kimi.ts`, `kimicode.ts`, `qwen.ts`, `sqlite-session-parser.ts` as a generic SQLite-session factory). Also has `classifier.ts`/`workflow-insights.ts` (real session/turn classification, richer than Lumen's spec'd approach) and `doctor.ts` (validated template for Lumen's unbuilt `DoctorEngine`). Fetch via `gh api repos/getagentseal/codeburn/contents/<path> -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw"`.
- **RTK** (`github.com/rtk-ai/rtk`, Apache-2.0, installed locally as `rtk`): a live command-interception proxy, different architecture from Lumen's post-hoc parsing, but its `parse_failures` SQLite table (`~/Library/Application Support/rtk/history.db`) is a validated pattern for durable malformed-input tracking that Lumen's `CRIT-LUMEN-025` claims to do (`"record a warning"`) but doesn't -- confirmed via direct code read that `claude.rs:60-66` just silently `continue`s on a parse error.
- **`ccusage`** (`github.com/ccusage/ccusage`, ~18k stars, hybrid TS/Rust monorepo): the single most directly comparable reference implementation found all session -- same input data AND same language (Rust) as Lumen. Real adapters at `rust/adapters/{claude,codex,opencode,gemini,kimi,qwen,amp,codebuff,copilot,droid,goose,grok,hermes,kilo,openclaw,pi,common}/src/`, shared allocation-conscious JSONL layer at `rust/adapters/common/src/jsonl.rs`. `opencode`'s adapter not yet read (would directly cross-check Lumen's already-verified real OpenCode findings) -- next thing to fetch if resuming this line of research.
- **Langfuse** (`github.com/langfuse/langfuse`, ~33k stars, MIT, YC W23): mature production OSS LLM observability platform. Real data model split across Postgres (`packages/shared/prisma/schema.prisma`, low-volume config) and ClickHouse (`packages/shared/clickhouse/migrations/`, high-volume trace/observation/score event data). Real OTel ingestion at `packages/shared/src/server/otel/{OtelIngestionProcessor,ObservationTypeMapper}.ts`.
- **OpenLLMetry** (`github.com/traceloop/openllmetry`, ~7.4k stars, Apache-2.0): real production OTel GenAI instrumentation. Anthropic instrumentation at `packages/opentelemetry-instrumentation-anthropic/opentelemetry/instrumentation/anthropic/span_utils.py`, MCP tool-span instrumentation at `packages/opentelemetry-instrumentation-mcp/`, migration/versioning history at `packages/opentelemetry-semantic-conventions-ai/MIGRATION.md`. `traceloop-sdk` (higher-level session/workflow wrapping) and the OpenAI/LangChain instrumentation packages not yet read -- open thread on whether `gen_ai.conversation.id` gets set one layer up from where it was checked.
- **OpenHands / `software-agent-sdk`** (`github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk`, Python -- note: the `OpenHands/OpenHands` repo itself is now only the frontend, confirmed via its own `AGENTS.md`, which documents a 5-repo split): the actual agent loop and native event model. `Event`/`Action`/`Observation` hierarchy at `openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/event/base.py`, delegation at `openhands-tools/.../delegate/impl.py`, stuck-detection at `openhands-sdk/.../conversation/stuck_detector.py`, persistence at `conversation/event_store.py`, compaction at `event/condenser.py`, native hook events at `event/hook_execution.py`. Sibling repos `OpenHands/agent-analysis`, `OpenHands/trajectory-visualizer`, `OpenHands/rubric`, `OpenHands/critic-rubrics`, `OpenHands/ToM-SWE` noticed but not investigated.
- **The real OTel GenAI semantic conventions spec itself**: `github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai`, attribute definitions at `model/gen-ai/registry.yaml`, span definitions at `model/gen-ai/spans.yaml` -- the opentelemetry.io docs page is only a redirect stub, fetch this repo directly, not the docs site.
